tone: Direct and unsentimental, with credibility earned through personal failure as often as expertise. Diagnoses problems plainly without condescension, and treats the reader as capable of acting on a clear insight.
sentence_rhythm: Predominantly short declarative sentences, often one thought per line. Frequently uses a two-beat structure where the second sentence reframes or sharpens the first, creating a cadence of claim followed by precision.
vocabulary_register: Plain professional with selective B2B marketing terminology (entity authority, AI engine, pipeline, demand gen). Avoids jargon that obscures; prefers concrete nouns and active verbs over abstractions and nominalizations.
recurring_arguments: Most B2B companies are invisible to AI search engines and have no awareness the problem exists
Content volume is not the answer; specificity and structure are what get cited by AI engines
Lead quality and brand problems are almost always content structure problems in disguise
Buyers finish most of their research before sales contact, increasingly through AI tools that don't show in analytics
The fix is faster than companies assume: days or weeks, not quarters or years
Distributed publishing across multiple surfaces beats single-channel content strategies
themes: AI search visibility and answer engine optimization
B2B buyer research behavior and the dark funnel
Content as answers versus content as audience-building
Entity authority and brand recognition in AI engines
The gap between knowing the right strategy and executing it
would_never_say: at the end of the day
post_structure_patterns: Opens with a sharp statistic, blunt personal admission, or provocative observation — no warm-up. Builds through a specific diagnosis that names the gap between what companies do and what works, often using a numbered list or contrast pair. Closes with a minimal concrete action or a reframing question, never a summary or motivational closer.
sample_phrases: The fix takes two weeks, not a year.
Not a lead quality problem. That's a content problem.
The volume game is over. The specificity game is just starting.
Brand gaps take years to close. Content gaps take weeks.
AI engines want the answer first.
If a buyer types this into Claude tomorrow, what do they get?
More work than a blog post. Less work than a lost deal.
They answer questions in the first sentence. No buildup.
